# Input File

```tsx
import { DownloadIcon, FileItem, IconFileFormat, InputFile, TrashIcon } from "@lucasdost/design-system"
```

An Upload Area to pick or drop files, above the File Item List. Without `multiple` it takes a single file: the Upload Area hides while there's a File Item, and comes back when it's removed. Mirrors the Figma Input File component, State (Default / Hover / Error / Disabled), and File Item, State (Loading / Uploaded / Error / Disabled).

## Example

From the Storybook story; names like `args` or `label` are the story controls.

```tsx
<InputFile {...args}>
  {args.multiple
    ? fileItems.map((_, index) => renderItem(index + 1))
    : renderItem(args.selectedItem ?? 1)}
</InputFile>
```

## Figma notes

Mirrors the Figma Input File and File Item components.
- Input File: State (Default / Hover / Error / Disabled). Hover comes from the browser, and dragging a file over the Upload Area looks the same; Error and Disabled come from props. Figma has no Read Only here.
- File Item: State (Loading / Uploaded / Error / Disabled). Items inside a disabled Input File are disabled too.
The Upload Area only hands over the files: the parent uploads them and renders one File Item per file as `children`. That's why the native input is emptied after each pick, and why it takes no form props like `name`. Without `multiple` it takes a single file: the Upload Area hides while there's a File Item, and comes back when it's removed. Figma's Upload, Download and Trash aren't drawn like the Hugeicons ones.

## Props

Documented props only; every component also accepts the props of the element or Base UI part it renders (`className`, events, ARIA…).

`IconFileFormat`:

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `format?` | `string` | The text in the tag, like "PDF" or "DOCX". |

`FileItemProps`:

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `state?` | `FileItemState` | Inside a disabled Input File, the state is always "disabled". |
| `description?` | `React.ReactNode` | Second line: the progress, the type and size, or the error. |
| `format?` | `string` | The text in the .Icon File Format tag. |
| `onDownload?` | `() => void` | Shows the Download button while Uploaded. |
| `onRemove?` | `() => void` | Shows the remove button while Uploaded. |
| `downloadLabel?` | `string` | Accessible name of the Download button. |
| `removeLabel?` | `string` | Accessible name of the remove button. |

`InputFileProps`:

| Prop | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `className?` | `string` | Classes for the root, around the label, Upload Area and File Item List. |
| `title?` | `React.ReactNode` | First line of the Upload Area. |
| `description?` | `React.ReactNode` | Second line of the Upload Area, usually the file limits. |
| `onFilesChange?` | `(files: File[]) => void` | Files picked or dropped that pass `accept` and `multiple`. |
| `onFilesRejected?` | `(files: File[]) => void` | Files dropped that don't pass `accept` or `multiple`. |
| `children?` | `React.ReactNode` | The File Item List: one `FileItem` per file. |

## Types

`FileItemProps`, `FileItemState`, `InputFileProps`

## Rules

- Import `DownloadIcon` from `@lucasdost/design-system`. Do not rebuild it with plain HTML and Tailwind classes.
- Style it through its props and variants first. Use `className` only for layout (margin, width, grid placement), never to change its colors, typography or radius.
- Colors come from the S0L tokens; see [color](../foundations/color.md).
